name: L9110S dual motor driver module
//: The blue two-channel breakout, also sold as HG7881: two SOP-8 chips, green screw terminals marked MOTOR A / MOTOR B, and a 6-pin header. What a host board has to provide is under `needs`; what is true of the part is under `facts`, each with where it came from.
//needs: What this part asks of the host, and the ONLY part of this file with a fixed shape. `signal` is the name the host will use; `pin` is what the module calls it. `needs` is what the host pin must be able to do, in the vocabulary assign_pins.py understands.

needs.note: PWM-capable host pin; direction and speed both live on the two inputs
the other half of the same channel

power.note: 2.5-12 V; this is the MOTOR supply, not logic

unused_pins.note: channel B is unused in a one-motor design and must not float — tie it to the driver's own ground

//facts: Deliberately open-ended. A motor driver's facts are input thresholds and current; a rangefinder's are an I2C address and a calibration. Forcing them into one schema produces a field nobody reads. Every entry says where it came from, and `verified` is false until someone has actually checked.

input_high_threshold_v.why_it_matters: ABSOLUTE, not ratiometric. If it were 0.7 x VCC it would be 4.2 V on a 6 V supply and 3.3 V logic would never turn the motor. This was checked precisely because the ratiometric reading would have killed the design.

continuous_current_a.source: 800 mA per channel, stated in the Handson guide's own description and in the GME/Eclipsera datasheet. Marketplace listings for 'L9110S' quote 500 mA, 800 mA, 1.5 A and 2.5 A — the name is a commodity rather than one part, so this is the figure for THIS module, not for anything sold under that name.

has_enable_pin.source: the module's own header: BIA BIB GND VCC AIA AIB
has_enable_pin.why_it_matters: There is no enable and no separate PWM pin, so the firmware has to encode direction and speed in the two inputs together.

onboard_input_pullups_ohms.source: Handson Technology L9110S module guide (document handson-l9110s-guide; also sold by GME/Eclipsera as 772-209), schematic on page 3: R2, R3, R4 and R5, all 10K, all to VCC
onboard_input_pullups_ohms.note: Read off the schematic rather than reported. All FOUR inputs are pulled up, so the module alone idles both channels high, which its truth table makes Off. But a host that adds its own 10k pulldown forms a divider at about VCC/2 — near 3 V on a 6 V supply, above this part's 2.5 V input-high threshold. Clones are built by many factories, so confirm on the module in hand: resistance from each input pin to VCC.

schematic_numbers_vcc_and_gnd_opposite_t.source: Handson Technology L9110S module guide (document handson-l9110s-guide; also sold by GME/Eclipsera as 772-209): the board photo on page 1 reads B-IA B-IB GND VCC A-IA A-IB along the header, while the P3 connector symbol on page 3 puts VCC on pin 3 and GND on pin 4
schematic_numbers_vcc_and_gnd_opposite_t.note: The silkscreen is the physical truth and is what pin_order follows. Recorded because anyone wiring from the schematic's pin numbers reverses the supply on a motor driver, and a vendor document disagreeing with its own board is exactly the kind of thing that is discovered twice.

//host_requirements: Things the host board must do that are not pins. Prose on purpose: these are design rules, and a rule nobody can read is not enforced.
host_requirements: Pull both inputs down in HARDWARE. The host's pins float for the ~300 ms between reset and firmware, and through any crash or reflash, and a floating CMOS input on an H-bridge can turn both halves on.

If a current shunt sits in this module's ground return, the module judges its inputs against ITS OWN ground, which the shunt lifts. Effective input high becomes (host logic level - I x R_shunt), and the margin over 2.5 V is what decides whether the motor turns under load.

body_mm.source: measured with calipers on the module in hand
body_mm.note: The header runs along one 29 mm edge and the screw terminals along the opposite one, so the body is NOT centred on the header.

pin_order_proof.source: Pad 1..N of the footprint, by this file's own pin names. Read directly off the silkscreen in the vendor's board photo — B-IA B-IB GND VCC A-IA A-IB — and corroborated by the Handson guide text, an archived Banana Robotics article and a Fritzing part. One reseller listing gives a different order and the vendor's own schematic symbol numbers VCC and GND the other way round, which is why this says where it came from.

wokwi.note: one channel: reads IA/IB and prints MOTOR: opening/closing/stopped; models no current, so a stall cannot be simulated

host_parts.why: the host's pins float for the ~300 ms between reset and firmware, and through any crash or reflash; a floating input can turn both halves of the bridge on
the same, for the other input: both held low is the only state that moves nothing
